title: Projects
text:
Exact standard errors for FOCE/FOCEI
Together with Mélissa Beldjenna, Matthew Fidler, Laura Zwep and Coen van Hasselt, I derived closed-form third-order sensitivity equations for the FOCE and FOCEI population likelihood. This gives the exact observed information, and therefore exact standard errors, without step-size dependent finite differencing. The method is implemented in nlmixr2. Read the preprint on bioRxiv: From exact gradients to exact standard errors: third-order sensitivity equations for the FOCE and FOCEI population likelihood.


admixr2 package
Pharmacometric modelling is traditionally performed using individual level data. Recently a new method was developed to fit pharmacometric models to summary level – or aggregate – data. This methodology allows for jointly modelling different data sources, once transformed into aggregate data. In this study we aimed to (1) implement this methodological framework into an accessible R package (admixr2, formerly admr) and (2) develop a novel algorithm with enhanced computational efficiency. The package allows calculating aggregate data from different data sources, jointly fitting one or multiple data sources and assessing model performance. The newly developed algorithm improves computational efficiency by iteratively reweighting internal Monte Carlo predictions. Three simulation scenarios using different data generating models demonstrated a 3 to 100-fold speed-up when using the novel Iterative Reweighting Monte Carlo (IR-MC) algorithm, while maintaining the convergence properties of the original MC algorithm. The IR-MC algorithm becomes increasingly efficient as model complexity rises, indicating its utility for more complex pharmacometric models.
The work is published in the Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics (doi:10.1007/s10928-025-10011-w); a preprint is available on bioRxiv. The package can be found on GitHub and on CRAN, with documentation at the package website.


Open-source development: nlmixr2 and ferx
I am a developer of the open-source pharmacometrics tools nlmixr2 (R, nonlinear mixed-effects modelling) and ferx, an NLME engine for population PK/PD with FOCEI, SAEM, analytical PK and ODE models.


Bayesian Statistics
In this project for the course Bayesian Statistics by Prof. dr. Herbert Hoijtink, the main goal was to develop a Gibbs sampler for a Bayesian linear regression model. By using two simulated data set the Gibbs sampler was tested and the results were compared. The Gibbs sampler was then applied to a real data set to identify the key factors that play a role in the University admittance process, using a open source data set. We used non-informative conjugate priors, as specified in the info note underneath. Next to this Bayesian Model Averaging was used to identify the most important variables in the model. The project was university coursework and was rewarded a 10.0/10.0 grade. The closed-form Bayesian engine (the Gibbs sampler and its derived conditional distributions) was written by hand, without AI-assisted coding. The project can be found here.

title: Hidde van de Beek
text:
Hi, I’m Hidde! I’m a PhD candidate in Pharmacometrics and Statistics at Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) under supervision of dr. Laura Zwep and Prof. dr. Coen van Hasselt. I graduated in June 2024 with a MSc in Methodology and Statistics at Utrecht University.
Currently I’m working on pharmacometric research in the field of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) in the LACDR. My research focusses on proper statistical methods for covariate model development and the usage of aggregate data in PKPD analysis. I published the R package admixr2 (formerly admr) for aggregate data population PK modelling (paper), I am a developer of nlmixr2 and ferx, and I recently posted a preprint on exact standard errors for FOCE/FOCEI.
In my free time I like to go hiking in Scotland, Norway, the Lake District, or anywhere else where I can find some mountains. Here I go back into the wild and enjoy the beautiful nature. I enjoy the bare necessities of life and the simplicity of the outdoors. My most recent bikepacking trip was to Italy, where I cycled from Rome to Como crossing the Apennines. My most recent hiking trip was Troms border trail at the Norwegian-Swedish-Finish border, where I hiked 150 km in 10 days through the summer-time arctic nature.
I used to row at U.S.R. Triton in Utrecht. Here I trained 10-12 times a week and competed in national and international competitions. My most beloved experience is reaching the semi-finals in the Temple eight of the Henley Royal Regatta in 2022. This one of the most prestigious rowing regattas in the world. Next to this, I won the prestigious Amstelbeker in 2024, a yearly national sprint competition for the best rowing clubs in the Netherlands.
